subject: biomedical-engineering
intro: Biomedical engineering leads into the medical technology industry — the engineers who turn physiology into devices, implants and diagnostics, and the scientists who test them.

roles.title: Bioengineers and Biomedical Engineers
roles.what: Apply knowledge of engineering, biology, chemistry, computer science and biomechanical principles to the design, development and evaluation of health systems and products — artificial organs, prostheses, instrumentation, medical information systems and care delivery systems.
roles.where: This is the course in miniature: physiology for engineers, biomaterials and implants, joint biomechanics, bioinstrumentation and biosignals, and the device design unit with its design controls and human factors.

roles.title: Medical Equipment Repairers
roles.what: Test, adjust or repair biomedical and electromedical equipment — the monitors, imaging systems and infusion devices hospitals depend on — keeping it safe and correctly calibrated for clinical use.
roles.where: Bioinstrumentation and biosignals — electrodes, amplifiers, ECG and EEG processing — plus the medical imaging physics topic teach you exactly the machines you will maintain, with sterilisation know-how from the device unit.

roles.title: Medical Scientists, Except Epidemiologists
roles.what: Conduct research dealing with the understanding of human diseases and the improvement of human health — clinical investigation, research and development, and studies that carry devices and therapies from bench to bedside.
roles.where: Cell and tissue engineering — culture, scaffolds, growth factors and mechanotransduction — and the frontiers unit on machine learning diagnostics and gene and cell therapy are the research toolkit this career extends.
